title: Proxmox cluster loses quorum after every power cut
author: nas_gardener
body: I run three NUCs in a Proxmox cluster and each time the power drops, two of them come back before the third and the cluster sits there without quorum until I log in and restart corosync by hand. Is there a sane way to make the nodes wait for each other, or should I just add a QDevice on the Raspberry Pi that is always on?

title: ZFS scrub taking 31 hours on 4x12TB raidz1, is that normal?
author: blockpointer
body: The pool is about 70 percent full and the scrub that used to finish overnight now runs for more than a day. SMART looks clean on all four drives. I noticed one disk reports much lower throughput in zpool iostat, so I am starting to suspect a bad SATA cable rather than the drive itself. What would you check first?

title: Finally got 10GbE working over the old Cat5e in my walls
author: copper_optimist
body: Everyone told me I would need to pull new cable, but two runs of roughly 18 metres negotiated at 10G without errors after I re-terminated the keystones. The third run only holds 2.5G. Posting the iperf numbers in case it helps someone decide whether to try before tearing the walls open.

title: Which UPS do you trust for a small rack?
author: voltdrop
body: My load is around 280 watts: a NAS, a switch, the router and one mini PC. I want at least fifteen minutes of runtime and a clean shutdown signal over USB that NUT understands. The APC units are easy to find here but the replacement batteries cost almost as much as the UPS. Any recommendations from people who have run one for a few years?

title: Pi-hole or AdGuard Home in 2026?
author: dnsdave
body: I have used Pi-hole since version 4 and it has been solid, but I keep reading that AdGuard Home handles encrypted upstreams and per-client rules without extra containers. For those who switched, was the migration of blocklists and local DNS records painful, and do you miss anything?
